Class AxisControlCommands

Namespace
TwinSharp.CNC
Assembly
TwinSharp.dll

Wraps the axis control commands of the HLI lr_mc_control control unit for a single CNC axis (gpAx[n].lr_mc_control.*), as described in section "Axis control commands" of the HLI documentation.

Every command in this class is an MC control unit with four elements:

  • enable_w — the PLC declares that it uses this control unit. The unit has no effect at all until this is TRUE, so call the matching ...Enable setter (or EnableAll()) once after connecting.
  • command_w — the value commanded by the PLC.
  • request_r — the value requested by a GUI communicating directly with the CNC. The PLC may accept the request by copying it into command_w, or ignore it.
  • state_r — the CNC acknowledgement, used to check whether the command took effect.

Other parts of lr_mc_control live in their own classes: AxisCoupling (axis_coupling), DistanceControl (distance_control) and ExternalAxisCommanding (add_cmd_values). The axis control commands that sit under ipo_mc_control (feedhold, override, reduced velocity, …) are not part of this class.

Precondition:PlcPresent must be set to true before the CNC accepts any HLI command for the axis.

ClearReferencePositionCommand

Clears the referenced state of an axis that was homed by setting the reference position or by G74. As long as this is true the axis is regarded as not referenced — which also temporarily switches off the software limit switches — and it can be marked as referenced again via SetReferencePositionCommand. Any offset activated by "set reference position" is not cleared. Writes clear_reference_position.command_w.

DeactivateAxisCommand

Deactivates (parks) the axis. While true the NC kernel does not signal drive errors, does not transfer HLI control bits to the drive, and a CNC reset does not trigger a drive reset. Moving a parked axis produces error P-ERR-70265. On PROFIDRIVE drives bit 0x80 is set in control word 2 (STW2). Writes deactivate_axis.command_w.

FeedEnableCommand

Axis-specific feed rate enable. Must be set for every axis that is to be moved, otherwise no path motion occurs. true = drive enable, false = drive STOP. On a true → false transition the drive is shut down in compliance with the acceleration parameters. With SERCOS drives this is derived from bit 13 of the control word. Writes release_feedhold.command_w.

SetReferencePositionCommand

Accept the reference position and mark the axis as referenced on a rising edge (false → true). The value the actual axis position is set to depends on P-AXIS-00278:

  • ABSOLUT — value of P-AXIS-00152.
  • OFFSET — drive encoder position + P-AXIS-00279.
  • PLC — value of ReferencePositionCommand.
  • PLC_OFFSET — drive encoder position + ReferencePositionCommand.
Works for axes with an absolute measuring system too. Writes set_reference_position.command_w. 
public bool SetReferencePositionCommand { get; set; }

TrackingModeCommand

Tracking mode. While true the control loop is open: the command value is set identical to the actual value read in, so the position lag becomes 0. Beware that an external force (for example the weight of the axis) can then slowly drift the axis position. Writes follow_up.command_w.

EnableAll()

Declares to the CNC that the PLC uses all axis control commands of this axis by setting every enable_w to true. Creates the ADS variable handles on first call — this is where AdsErrorCode 1808 will surface if the HLI is not available on the target.
